title: Remoteness limits recovery to damage sufficiently connected with the tort

content.overview: Remoteness limits recovery to damage sufficiently connected with the tort. Modern law asks whether the kind of damage was reasonably foreseeable; an intervening event may break causation in appropriate circumstances.
content.study:
Remoteness limits recovery to damage sufficiently connected with the tort. Modern law asks whether the kind of damage was reasonably foreseeable; an intervening event may break causation in appropriate circumstances.\
\
Re Polemis used a direct-consequence approach; The Wagon Mound shifted the common-law test toward reasonable foreseeability. Hughes v Lord Advocate shows that the precise manner of occurrence need not be foreseeable if the kind of damage was foreseeable.
